role: Crash-safety net for raw RR beats: writes every recording's beats to RRBackup/ in the App Group container (one-shot encrypted single-file JSON, or append-only header+JSONL via RawRRBackup+Streaming.swift), keeps a JSON index of backups, and serves retrieve/list/discard/purge/reconcile APIs to recovery, archive and diagnostics code.
types: RawRRBackup: class (@unchecked Sendable) — raw RR backup store, conforming to SealableBackupStore (RawBackupSealer.swift) so its sealer repairs its files; extended by two in-file extensions (holdsBackup, writeOneShot and the SealableBackupStore conformance; fileprivate backupFileSize), RawRRBackup+Streaming.swift, RawRRBackup+IndexRecovery.swift, RawRRBackup+Reconciliation.swift (beat-count and archived-flag reconciliation, markAsArchived) and SessionStorageDiagnostic.swift
RawRRBackup.BackupEntry: struct (Codable) — decoded backup (id, captureDate, deviceId, points, hash)
RawRRBackup.BackupHeader: struct (Codable) — header file of the append-only format
RawRRBackup.BackupIndex: struct (Codable) — index row (fileName for one-shot, backedUpCount for append-only, archived flag, lastBackupTime) with schemaVersion key
RawRRBackup.TerminationForensicsSummary: struct — static lockless view of one index row for CrashLogManager
state: file:{AppGroup group.com.chrissharp.flowrecovery or Documents or tmp}/RRBackup/ (AppConfig.backupDirectoryName)
file:RRBackup/<uuid>_<stamp>.json (one-shot backup, stamp = write time in ms raised past any taken name; older files carry whole seconds; encrypted when EncryptionManager available)
file:RRBackup/<uuid>_header.json, file:RRBackup/<uuid>_points.jsonl (append-only format; point lines sealed by EncryptionManager when the key is reachable)
mem:RawRRBackup.sealer (RawBackupSealer for backupDirectory: ledger-aware one-shot writes and the re-encryption repair)
mem:RawRRBackup.indexSaveOwed (set while an index save has thrown since the last one that landed; guarded by indexLock)
mem:RawRRBackup.unlockObservers (NotificationTokens: protectedDataDidBecomeAvailable / didBecomeActive observers, removed in deinit)
mem:RawRRBackup.notificationCenter (where the unlock and activation observers are added; NotificationCenter.default for init(directory:) and init())
mem:RawRRBackup.repairQueued (OSAllocatedUnfairLock<Bool>: a repairAfterUnlock queued and not yet started)
toplevel: Stored-property initializers: index = [], indexReadFailed = false, indexSaveOwed = false, unlockObservers = NotificationTokens(), fileManager = FileManager.default, indexLock = NSLock(), appendQueue serial utility queue, lineEncoder closure; sealer is set in init(directory:). The second in-file extension declares the SealableBackupStore conformance. BackupIndex declares CodingKeys including schemaVersion. The class is @unchecked Sendable relying on indexLock + appendQueue; only incrementalBackup, resetInMemoryStateAfterPurge, reencryptPendingBackups, repairAfterUnlock, reconcileIndexInBackground, discardBackup and purgeOldBackups run on appendQueue — backup(), markAsArchived, reconcileArchived and reconcileBeatCount mutate index under indexLock only. A save that throws leaves indexSaveOwed set; saveIndexIfOwed retries it on the next incremental backup or unlock repair.

Unless a repair is already queued and not yet started (repairQueued.setIfClear), queues one asynchronously on appendQueue (behind any append in flight, so no points file is rewritten while it is appended to). When it starts it clears repairQueued, so a call made while it runs queues the next; then it retries an index save a failed write left owed (saveIndexIfOwed; a failure is logged by attempt and stays owed), and hands this store to the sealer's repair pass (RawBackupSealer.reencryptPending), which with the key reachable reseals every backup queued in the raw-backup ledger.

One-shot backup: refuses empty points; via replaceableIndexEntry merges an index the launch could not read (throws while unreadable) and refuses to replace an existing backup with more beats; builds the entry (captureDate = caller's, else the existing row's, else now; integrityHash); notes whether the session was queued for re-encryption (RawBackupSealer.isPending); writeOneShot writes it under a never-reused <uuid>_<ms>.json name and replaces and saves the index row (on a failed save the previous row is restored and the new file removed); only then deletes the session's append-only files and the previous one-shot file (sealer.removeReplacedFile, which queues the session again when a possibly-plaintext old file will not go). Returns the entry.

Asynchronously on appendQueue (behind any append, so no append runs during a rewrite): hands this store to the sealer's repair pass (RawBackupSealer.reencryptPending), which, when the raw-backup ledger has pending ids and encryption is available, repairs each pending backup: its plain one-shot files and the plain lines of its points files.

units.does: Computes the cutoff keepDays (default 90) ago and runs purgeArchivedBackups synchronously on appendQueue: archived backups captured before it lose their files and rows, except a backup with a file still on disk, which keeps its row.

On appendQueue: for each archived row captured before cutoff, removes every file of the session (removedEveryFile); drops only the rows whose files all went, saves the index and logs how many of the old backups were purged. A backup with a file left keeps its row, so nothing is orphaned.
removeEveryFile through attempt: true when every file of the session went; a failure is logged and gives false.

Removes every one-shot file of the session (OneShotBackupName.files, indexed or not) and its append files (appendFiles: header, points, set-aside points) via BackupFiles.remove, then clears the session from the rawBackup re-encryption queue (PendingEncryptionLedger.clear), since no plaintext of it is left. Throws when the folder cannot be listed, or BackupError.couldNotRemove naming the files still on disk, leaving it queued.

If reindex's index save throws (reindex has already restored the previous row in memory), removes the new, unindexed file and rethrows, so the restored row still names its own intact file with its own hash. Returns the file name.
